name: grill-with-docs
description: Grill a plan against the domain model. Sharpen terminology, update GLOSSARY.md and ADRs as decisions crystallize.

steps.name: Scan documentation
steps.instruction: Read CLAUDE.md for doc layout. Scan for glossary, ADRs, scope, conventions, architecture, testing, rule catalogue, endpoint registries. Create files lazily.
checklist: CLAUDE.md read, existing docs + catalogue + registries identified

steps.name: Catalogue-driven grill
steps.instruction: If rule catalogue exists: follow reference/catalogue-grill.md. Per-family checklist, grill depth-first. Consolidated decision-tree ADRs (target 6-8). Cross-reference catalogue open items. Never cut features/endpoints without user approval.
checklist: Each family grilled, open items addressed

steps.name: Interview
steps.instruction: One question at a time, with recommended answer. Explore codebase instead of asking when possible. Challenge terms against glossary. Sharpen vague language to canonical terms. Probe edge cases with scenarios. Cross-reference claims with code.
checklist: Every design branch walked, terms validated against glossary
Architecture questions grilled against constraint sheet

steps.name: Update docs inline
steps.instruction: Update GLOSSARY.md inline when term resolved, not batched. No implementation details in glossary. Cascade to existing docs when genuine: naming -> NAMING.md, scope -> SCOPE.md, deps -> ARCHITECTURE.md, tests -> TESTING.md. Never create docs just to cascade.
checklist: Terms written to GLOSSARY.md immediately, cascades applied to existing docs

steps.name: Offer ADRs sparingly
steps.instruction: ADR only when all three hold: (1) hard to reverse, (2) surprising without context, (3) real trade-off. Consolidate related decisions into single ADR. Structure with constraint sheet: workload, state, trust, operations, rejected alternative, revisit trigger.
checklist: Three-gate test applied, ADRs consolidated with constraint sheet structure

tone: Adversarial but constructive - stress the plan against the domain model.
